newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU's 1997 pork output seen down due to swine fever.
newsitem.headline: EU's 1997 pork output seen down due to swine fever.

text.p: Some 184 million pigs will be slaughtered for human consumption in the European Union in 1997 compared with 191 million in 1996 amid outbreaks of swine fever, a report from Germany's farm price office ZMP said.
The forecast was based on the assumption that the contagious disease, which does not affect humans, was mostly under control and not spreading much outside the Netherlands.
In the Netherlands, supplies of pigs for slaughter and live exports should be down by 40 percent from normal levels, ZMP said. By the end of the year, they should still be down by 25 percent.
Pig carcase sales from Dutch producers in 1997 were likely to be down by 30 percent, or by seven million animals, when compared with a normal year, ZMP said.
